messages:
anita: Quick follow-up from the tri-mode adapter RFC: we need a firm proposal for telemetry/headers that handles origin, fallback, and model info without exploding cardinality. I sketched something, want feedback.

sam: Nice. TL;DR request: metrics must be low-cardinality; traces can carry richer info but only when sampled and permissioned.

dave: Agreed. Operationally we need a minimal set of tags that answer SLO questions: hosting_mode, route_path, variant_bucket, routing_version, and fallback_reason. Keep all tag values finite.

anita: Proposed enums: hosting_mode=HOSTED|DEDICATED|PRIVATE ; route_path=PREFERRED|FALLBACK|SAFE_DEGRADED ; variant_bucket=perf|balanced|accurate ; fallback_reason=none|capacity|model_mismatch|auth|quota. routing_version is free-form but limited to short tokens (v1, v2).

mike (security): Important: no tenant identifiers in hosted metrics. For Private mode we can include tenant context but only to the customer-controlled audit store. Any traces carrying PII must be opt-in per customer contract.

sam: Implementation idea: propagate via lightweight headers on each handoff so adapters and runtime can annotate the request early. Header names (draft):
```http
X-RW-Hosting-Mode: DEDICATED
X-RW-Route-Path: FALLBACK
X-RW-Variant-Bucket: perf
X-RW-Routing-Version: v2
X-RW-Fallback-Reason: capacity
X-RW-Telemetry-Sample: 1/500
```
This keeps metrics simple but lets sampled traces include richer model_name or variant_id (only when allowed).

dave: For variant_bucket mapping: runtime should own a mapping table from concrete model name -> bucket. That mapping is a config blob (controlled rollout) so we don't suddenly add millions of tag values when new model names appear.

anita: How should we treat private deployments where customers want full model names in their internal metrics? Proposal: hosted metrics enforce low-cardinality buckets; Private deployments get a config toggle to emit higher-cardinality tags but only into their self-hosted metrics pipeline. Public/hosted backends must never ingest high-cardinality model names.

mike (security): +1. Also add TTL for sampled trace payloads by default (30 days) and require explicit retention exceptions for compliance. Record the opt-in flow in the RFC.

sam: Edge case: adapter fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated -> private). Need a deterministic precedence for tagging so dashboards don't double-count. I propose the first non-NONE hosting_mode wins and route_path should be set to the most degraded step (if a request used fallback at any stage mark FALLBACK).

dave: Good call. Also include numeric routing_version so we can correlate across releases (int or short token). Keep it small.

anita: Migration plan notes: 1) runtime emits headers with default values (hosting=UNKNOWN,path=PREFERRED,variant_bucket=balanced,fallback_reason=none). 2) adapters adopt mapping table and override fields as needed. 3) dashboards migrate to new metric naming: redwood.request.latency_ms{hosting_mode="...",route_path="...",variant_bucket="..."}. 4) remove any dashboards that reference raw model names.

mike (security): I'll draft the telemetry policy blurb: allowed fields in hosted metrics vs audit sinks, sampling opt-in process, and private deployment exceptions.

ops-bot: Reminder: small runtime push window next Wed 01:00-03:00 UTC. Tag @sam if you want it.

sam: I'll take the slot. I'll open a PR for the header emit patch and the mapping table API.

anita: Action items then: anita: update RFC with header schema + mapping semantics; sam: PR and test plan; dave: dashboard migration checklist; mike: telemetry policy text. I'll post an updated RFC patch by EOD tomorrow.

dave: One more nit: instrument the metrics exporter to drop any unexpected tag values (emit "other") and log an alert so we can catch regressions early.

anita: Excellent. That prevents accidental metric cardinality leaks. Thanks everyone.
